flags.title: Brand deal without an Ad label
flags.evidence: You say "VitaBoost sent me these" and show the code PRIYA20 for ₹200 off, but there is no "Ad" or "Collaboration" label on screen or in the caption.

citation.title: Guidelines for Influencer Advertising in Digital Media

sourceQuote.text: If the advertiser or its agents gives free or discounted products or service, or other perks, and then the influencer mentions one of its products or services, a disclosure is needed even if they were not specifically asked to talk about that product or service.

flags.suggestedFix: Put "Ad" on screen for at least a third of the video (about 20 seconds here) and start your caption with it.

flags.title: Supplement shown as treating diabetes
flags.evidence: "My sugar is under control since I started this, I barely need my diabetes tablets now" links the product to treating diabetes, a condition in the Act's Schedule.

citation.title: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954

flags.suggestedFix: Drop the diabetes line. Talk about your routine, not about treating a condition, and never suggest cutting prescribed medicine.
